q: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the thermal capacity (or) heat capacity of the object.
e: True. The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the thermal capacity (or) heat capacity of the object. Heat capacity is the heat to raise the whole sample by 1 K, C = Q/Δθ.

q: The thermal capacity of an object is given by the formula $C = \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta T}$.
e: True. The thermal capacity of an object is given by the formula C = (ΔQ)/(ΔT). Keep the symbols and the sign in that relation.

q: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is joule per kelvin ($J K^{-1}$).
e: True. In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is joule per kelvin (J K^-1). Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts.

q: The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a type of the material it is made of.
e: True. The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a type of the material it is made of. thermal has to stay in that role in the sentence.

q: An object having lower thermal capacity can be heated up easily.
e: True. An object having lower thermal capacity can be heated up easily. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: Water has a relatively low thermal capacity.
e: False. Swap low for high and the physics lines up.

q: Because of high thermal capacity, water is used to cool engines.
e: True. Because of high thermal capacity, water is used to cool engines. Because has to stay in that role in the sentence.

q: In cold countries, water is used to store heat in solar heating system of the houses.
e: True. In cold countries, water is used to store heat in solar heating system of the houses. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: Suppose that the internal energy of $n$ moles of a substance changes by $\Delta Q$ due to the temperature change $\Delta T$.
e: True. Suppose that the internal energy of n moles of a substance changes by ΔQ due to the temperature change ΔT. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule.

q: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is molar thermal capacity.
e: True. The thermal capacity for 1 mole is molar thermal capacity. thermal has to stay in that role in the sentence.

q: The formula for molar thermal capacity is $C = \frac{\Delta Q}{n \Delta T}$.
e: True. The formula for molar thermal capacity is C = (ΔQ)/(n ΔT). Keep the symbols and the sign in that relation.

q: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per kelvin ($J \text{ mol}^{-1} K^{-1}$).
e: True. SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per kelvin (J mol^-1 K^-1). Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts.
